Chery Group International User Summit Features the World Premiere of the All-New Omoda X Adventurer
12 photos
Photo: Omoda Jaecoo Australia
The Chery Group International User Summit allowed the sibling brands Omoda Jaecoo to also take center stage during the event, and Omoda launched X, its newest adventure SUV.
Subdivisions of Chery International, part of the Chery Automobile group, a Chinese vehicle manufacturer, Omoda and Jaecoo have been established since 2022 as sibling brands that only sell vehicles outside of China. Omoda and Jaecoo entered various international regions a little later: Australia in 2023, Europe in 2024, and South Africa or Mexico also in 2023.
Now, Omoda Jaecoo are a constant presence in Australia , where they have deals with entities like Uber for their drivers to use the eligible vehicles, constantly receive various awards like the Jaecoo J5 EV being recognized in the 2026 Australian Good Design Awards, partner with the Red Bull Wings Cup, or bring together owners with the My OJ Club.
They also don’t neglect new model introductions, and back in September the company announced two all-new Omoda SUVs for Australia: Omoda 4 and Omoda 7, which are coming in 2027 below the Omoda 9 flagship after they were unveiled locally at Everything Electric Sydney. Now, at the recent Chery Group International User Summit, Omoda Jaecoo also hosted Omoda X Night, which was an event dedicated to the global reveal of Omoda’s latest model dubbed “X”.
The new model is a true ‘crossover’: it strives to combine the “everyday practicality of an SUV, the adventurous spirit of an off-road vehicle and the dynamic character of a sports car.” Omoda wants to expand the possibilities of its CUV range and bring a new automotive choice for adventure-focused customers.
The model’s design seeks inspiration from the futuristic ‘mecha culture’, according to the company, and the Omoda X “brings power, technology and a vision of the future into its design.” The designers cooked up a wide-body stance featuring “broad shoulders, a tightly sculpted waistline and a sporty silhouette,” all to create “a sense of power.”
The new model is also positioned below the Omoda 9 and measures 4,650 mm (183 inches) in length, 1,910 mm (75.19 inches) in width, and has a height of 1,720 mm or 67.71 inches. To support its adventure-focused design, the new CUV has 19-inch alloy wheels with rugged all-terrain tires, 200 mm or 7.87 inches of ground clearance, and can go through areas of water thanks to its wading depth of over 700 mm (27.55 inches). Also, towing capacity is 1,800 kg or 3,968 pounds, while inside there are no less than 39 storage spaces “providing more room for equipment for outdoor activities.”
The cabin has the so-called ‘Mecha Command Cockpit’, featuring a twin-wing layout and X-shaped floating center console. There is a 10.25-inch digital instrument cluster and a 13.2-inch central touchscreen, but the Chinese have also listened to customers, and physical controls are available for AC and driving modes, for example. Both 2WD and AWD options will be offered, alongside EV and PHEV powertrains.
